the synthesis of a novel series of 2-imino- and 2-oxo-pyridine derivatives, and their in vitro evaluation for their PDE3A inhibitory and anticancer activities.

the prepared compounds are potential anticancer agents and PDE3 inhibitors, which could be used as lead compounds in further development of anticancer drugs and PDE3 modulators.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2-imino derivatives are more potent than 2-oxo derivatives in both enzyme inhibition and tumor cell growth inhibitions.
the 4,6-disubstituted-2-imino-dihydropyrindines are more potent PDE3 inhibitors than the 4, 6-disubstitued-2-oxodihydropyrimidines.
the 4,6-disubstituted 2-oxo or 2-imino-3-carbonitile derivatives are a new series of potential anticancer agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 4,6-disubstituted-2-imino-pyridine-1,2,3-tricarbonitrile moiety is a promising lead structure for further anticancer drug design.
the 6,4-diarylpyridines are promising lead compounds for the development of novel anticancer agents and/or PDE3 inhibitors.
the 4,6-disubstituted 2-imino-3-cyano-1,2 dihydropyridine scaffold can be used as a template for the development of novel anticancer agents.
